speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of walking unsteadily and appearing "drunk," along with clumsiness specifically on the right side, suggest a problem in the right cerebellum or its connecting pathways. Given your significant medical history, have you ever been diagnosed with conditions like stroke, multiple sclerosis, or heavy alcohol use?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, I need to urgently evaluate for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) or other immune-mediated demyelination. Please confirm if you have experienced any recent headaches, vision changes, or seizures.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)

The MRI confirms multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, which is the classic radiological presentation of PML. Given your immunosuppression from natalizumab and Crohn's disease, this is a known opportunistic infection, not a relapse of Multiple Sclerosis.
